records.title: F-15EX: a production recovery is not yet a monthly acceptance series
records.decision: Qualify; bring the retained timing discrepancy into the current narrative
records.rationale: The four-section case correctly separates production, delivery, arrival, formal acceptance and readiness, and does not admit a monthly series. Its first paragraph still repeats the issuer’s less-than-three-weeks sequence without the later retained December 11 arrival qualification. The assigned September 25 notice already records that discrepancy, but the current narrative should carry it directly. Reproducibility remains necessary; a second human is not a prerequisite under the owner policy.

findings.finding: Keep the August 4–November 17 interruption and deliveries during that interval attributed to the issuer. Add the later official-copy and receiving-wing timing conflict without pretending the two sources necessarily use the same milestone.

An identifier is not a cumulative count. Factory completion, government transfer, physical arrival and readiness can have different dates. No throughput, on-time fraction or fleet-readiness series follows from selected deliveries.

Require the full identity-linked acceptance population, revisions, rework and actual zero-acceptance periods before a numerical series. Do not claim that missing months equal zero or that a second person has reviewed anything.

required_presentational_changes.prior: The Air Force account attributes a production-line halt from August 4 to November 17, 2025 to a strike at Boeing’s St. Louis facility. It also reports EX14 delivery on August 19, EX15 on November 16 and EX16 less than three weeks later. The article therefore describes deliveries within the stated production-halt interval; it does not say that every delivery activity stopped. These are the issuer’s stated events and attribution, not an independently reconstructed production ledger.

It also reports EX14 delivery on August 19, EX15 on November 16 and EX16 less than three weeks later. The article therefore describes deliveries within the stated production-halt interval; it does not say that every delivery activity stopped. records.title: Victorian Big Battery: keep the incident and the service in the same history
records.decision: Accept the dated incident-and-service narrative with no current reliability finding
records.rationale: All four sections maintain the July 30 fire, August 2 control and August 3 investigation chronology, then separately attribute the February 2023 service description. Capacity, reserved transmission support and market participation are not confused with energy output, current availability or household benefits. The case neither invents a final cause nor treats later operation as proof that every failure mechanism was eliminated.

findings.finding: Keep two affected packs and the then-unfinished investigation attributed to the rolling CFA account. No final cause, complete remediation or September 2026 condition is established.

300 MW asset description, up-to-250 MW virtual-transmission role and 50 MW summer/300 MW other-time market participation are not additive independent assets or measured energy delivery. February 2, 2023 remains the page date.

Neither the incident nor later service proves universal battery failure/success. Availability needs its own eligible intervals, obligations, outages and configuration; bills and avoided outages need receiving-population and comparator evidence.
